title: Kiosk blocked-item recovery
lede: A blocked scan now explains the next safe move instead of leaving the operator at a dead end.

stats.n: Three choices on a timing-resolvable conflict row
Scanned items remain staged while the operator recovers

sections.heading: Blocked checkout scan stage
sections.note: Same availability-conflicts DEBUG fixture, same four-item cart, and the same iPad Air 11-inch (M4) simulator viewport. The before capture is the inspected pre-recovery state from the preceding availability-status slice.

pairs.title: When the camera is already reserved
pairs.sub: Look beneath each blocked cart row for the operator's next move.
pairs.beforeCap: The row identifies the reservation and still has a small remove control, but changing the return time or trying another item is left to operator inference.
pairs.afterCap: Each blocking row now has a dedicated What now? band with Remove item, Change return time, and Scan another item; the blocked row remains staged until the operator chooses.

changes.h: A blocked scan now has an explicit recovery path
changes.was: After understanding who held the item and when it was due back, the operator still had to decide how to recover from the blocked add.
changes.now: A timing-resolvable conflict row presents three direct choices: remove the staged item, edit the return time, or re-arm scanning for another item/unit; other blocking states show the applicable safe subset.

changes.h: Changing the return time keeps availability trustworthy
changes.was: A populated cart could return from checkout details without a clearly documented fresh availability check for the new due time.
changes.now: The cart is preserved while details reopen, and returning to scanning refreshes availability against the edited return time before completion can proceed.

verification: Focused source contracts: 10/10 passing across the actionable-availability, availability-status, reservation-battery-list, numbered-battery-rendering, and reservation-pickup suites.
Native gates: WisconsinKiosk Debug and Release builds pass for the iPad Air 11-inch (M4), iOS 26.5 simulator; project parity, drift, and iOS gap audits pass.
Visual: the matched before/after captures were inspected after installing the fresh Debug build; the after capture shows the new controls on both blocked rows.
Repository docs: npm run verify:docs remains blocked by pre-existing generated codemap drift in dirty parallel files, which was preserved rather than regenerated.
notes: This is local source/build/simulator proof only. Physical managed-iPad interaction with the real scanner/camera and production deployment remain open gates.

The before image is the previously captured, inspected availability-status result for the same availability-conflicts fixture and viewport, reused as the exact pre-recovery baseline rather than reconstructed by hand.

Scan another item/unit intentionally leaves the blocked row staged; Remove item is the explicit action that removes it. No API, schema, permission, allocation, audit, or transactional completion contract changed.
